The `setSelected` method in the `OptionGroup` class is responsible for selecting an option within the group. It sets the `selected` field based on the provided `Option` object. 

From the code snippet of the `setSelected` method, it appears that if the selected option is `null`, the `selected` field is reset to `null`. If no option has been previously selected or the same option is being reselected, the `selected` field is set to the `opt` value of the provided `Option`.

The issue may be related to how the `selected` field is being set when the provided `Option` object does not have a short name. It is possible that the comparison in `selected.equals(option.getOpt())` may not handle long options correctly, causing the `selected` field to not be set as expected.

Next, I will provide a step-by-step diagnosis of the bug based on the information gathered so far.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `GnuParserTest.testOptionGroupLong` is designed to verify the selection of an option with a long name within an `OptionGroup`. However, the bug report indicates that selecting an option without a short name in the group does not work correctly. The `OptionGroup.setSelected` method is responsible for setting the selected option based on the provided `Option` object. The comparison `selected.equals(option.getOpt())` in the `setSelected` method may not handle long options correctly, leading to the `selected` field not being set as expected when the option has no short name. This mismatch in option comparison logic likely causes the failure observed in the test case.

I recommend investigating and updating the comparison logic in the `OptionGroup.setSelected` method to correctly handle options without short names.
